prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital automated medication dispensing/returns: order intake, pharmacy prep/verification, cold chain, tube transport, ward cabinets, returns, dose exceptions. Aliases: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Elements: Gateway (validates patient/product/dose/route/timing before downstream release; rejects incomplete/inconsistent updates, retains reason; Order Reconciliation Snapshot; routes to review). Robot (uses Snapshot to compare requested qty vs dispense events/cabinet balances by stable order ID; retains order details, checks active/authorization; Priority Refill Tote Tag; presents package to Station; on exception stops pick, holds package, preserves scan data). Station (compares order vs scanned product/strength/qty, blocks on mismatch; Batch Release Note; Dose Exception Review Slip). Cooler (temperature records; reports excursions/connectivity loss; affected stock unavailable pending assessment). East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles (route availability; capsules; Tube Route Exception Ticket). Pneumatic Tube Network (compliant loads; segment unavailable until tested). North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers (states Ready for Dispense, Out of Service; North confirms ward via tote tag, blocks held transactions; South reports failed lock/unrecognized access). Return Kiosk (Return Bin Audit Label). Actors: Clinical Pharmacist (Review Slip; approves/rejects; if inconclusive keeps hold, seeks higher-level decision). Pharmacy Technician (prep; Cold Chain Handoff Card; confirms no unresolved reconciliation discrepancy before routine replenishment; no clinical decisions). Medication Safety Officer (reviews diversion, repeated high-risk exceptions, harm events; sends Diversion Review Packet to IT Operations Specialist). IT Operations Specialist (checks access/transaction/device logs without changing disposition; investigates software/connectivity faults, records findings). Biomedical Engineer (evaluates mechanical/sensor faults, advises return to service). Registered Nurse (verifies ward loads, returns; keeps holds; escalates to Pharmacist). Charge Nurse (Cabinet Downtime Notice; assigns open issues across handover). Hospital Courier (Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record). Requirements: discrepancies (patient/medication/qty) hold until resolved; cancelled excluded; corrected = new authoritative version; duplicates flagged not added; partials conservative; timestamps/transaction IDs kept; reconciliation outcome records matched values, differences,

New part:
S161: North Ward Cabinet Controller applies the North Ward medication access rules when evaluating a cabinet transaction.
S162: Its ward-specific configuration defines permitted medication locations, access roles, and transaction limits for each cabinet.
S163: The configuration associates each medication location with the product identifiers and quantity thresholds used by the ward.
S164: Cabinet availability is calculated from the last confirmed inventory count and subsequent recorded movements.
S165: Configured maximum and minimum quantities guide replenishment decisions without overriding an active clinical restriction.
S166: Access rules require an authenticated user role appropriate to the requested medication and transaction type.
S167: High-risk medication locations can require an additional confirmation before a removal is accepted.
S168: The controller rejects a transaction when its location mapping does not match the reconciled medication identity.
S169: Configuration changes are versioned, reviewed, and recorded with the effective time and approving authority.
S170: If the controller has not received a current approved configuration, it prevents routine dispensing and reports the condition for investigation.
S171: Bluejay maintains a time-stamped temperature history for each refrigerated medication compartment and raises an alarm when a configured limit is exceeded.
S172: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler applies approved upper and lower temperature limits to each monitored compartment.
S173: Calibrated probes report readings at configured intervals, and the cooler records probe identity and calibration status with each reading.
S174: Refrigerated stock is identified by medication, lot, and expiration date so that each unit remains traceable to its storage history.
S175: When readings exceed a limit or a probe becomes unavailable, the affected stock is marked ineligible for routine dispensing.
S176: The cooler preserves the affected stock in its current controlled environment while the condition is assessed.
S177: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler uses the handoff card to compare a transfer’s recorded custody time with its temperature history.
S178: A Clinical Pharmacist reviews excursion details and determines whether affected stock may be released, quarantined, or discarded under pharmacy policy.
S179: The cooler retains the disposition status against the affected lot and prevents stock marked ineligible from being selected for routine dispensing.
S180: Authorized access to refrigerated compartments is recorded with the user identity, access time, and affected stock identifiers.
S181: Door-open duration is monitored so that an access event that threatens temperature control can be distinguished from a brief inspection.
S182: Temperature alarms remain active during loss of network connectivity, and local records are retained until communication is restored.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
